summary: 1 critical, 2 major, 0 minor issues found in pretool-bash-safety.sh

checks.name: Line 287: /usr/bin/happy\b vs /usr/bin/happy-dev
checks.details: CRITICAL BUG: The pattern '(^|[;&|]\s*)/usr/bin/happy\b' on line 287 uses \b (word boundary). In both grep -E and Python re, \b fires between a word char [a-zA-Z0-9_] and a non-word char. The hyphen '-' is NOT a word char, so \b matches between 'y' and '-' in 'happy-dev'. This means /usr/bin/happy-dev is incorrectly blocked by this rule. Verified with: echo 'abc-def' | grep -qE 'abc\b' returns match=true. Line 316 already uses the correct pattern happy([^-]|$) for the same purpose, proving the fix is known.

checks.name: Line 287: bare 'happy' vs 'happy-dev' command
checks.details: Pattern '(^|[;&|]\s*)happy\s+(daemon|--version|auth)\b' requires a space after 'happy' (\s+). 'happy-dev daemon start' has a hyphen not a space after 'happy', so it does NOT match. This is correct.

checks.name: Line 307-308: write protection /usr/bin/happy vs happy-dev
checks.details: Line 307 catches writes to /usr/bin/happy (substring match catches happy-dev too), but line 308 has an explicit exception: '! echo $COMMAND | grep -qE /usr/bin/happy-dev'. So 'cp foo /usr/bin/happy' is blocked, 'cp foo /usr/bin/happy-dev' is allowed. This is correct. Also correctly blocks writes to /usr/lib/node_modules/happy and /usr/lib/node_modules/happy-coder (the actual production package name) since both match the substring.

checks.name: Line 316: happy([^-]|$) pattern (reference implementation)
checks.details: Line 316 uses '/usr/bin/happy([^-]|$)' which is the CORRECT pattern. It matches '/usr/bin/happy --version' (space after happy) and '/usr/bin/happy' (end of string), but does NOT match '/usr/bin/happy-dev'. This pattern should be used on line 287 too.

checks.name: Kill PID blocking completeness
checks.details: Two rules cover kill: line 161 blocks 'kill -9' (any kill -9), line 297 blocks 'kill [0-9]' (kill followed by bare PID number). However, 'kill -TERM 12345', 'kill -15 12345', and 'kill -HUP 12345' all escape BOTH rules. Line 161 only catches -9 specifically. Line 297 requires a digit immediately after 'kill\s+', but '-TERM' and '-15' start with a hyphen, not a digit. The PID appears after the signal flag and is not caught.

checks.name: npm install -g blocking completeness
checks.details: Line 276 pattern 'npm\s+install\s+-g' and 'npm\s+install\s+--global' requires -g/--global immediately after 'install'. Two bypass variants: (1) 'npm install happy-coder -g' puts the flag after the package name, (2) 'npm i -g happy-coder' uses the 'i' shorthand instead of 'install'. Neither is caught.

checks.name: curl session creation blocking
checks.details: Line 265 correctly blocks curl/wget POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to /v1/sessions, /v1/machines, /session-started, /spawn-session. GET requests (no -X POST or -d flag) are correctly allowed.

checks.name: Docker build production URL blocking
checks.details: Lines 207-219 block Dockerfile.webapp builds without HAPPY_SERVER_URL and block cluster-fluster URL. Production vs dev URL distinction is handled by project-level hook (pretool-block-production.sh), not this global hook.

checks.name: any_subcmd_matches function (dead code)
checks.details: Function defined at line 25 but never called anywhere in the hook. Dead code, not a security issue.

checks.name: docker-compose down/restart pattern
checks.details: Line 140 pattern 'docker.compose\s+(down|restart)' uses dot which matches any char, covering both 'docker compose' and 'docker-compose' forms.

checks.name: Docker container stop/restart whitelist
checks.details: Lines 130-137 use check_docker_targets_all_dev which verifies every container name in the command is in the DEV_CONTAINERS whitelist (happy-web-dev only). Non-dev containers like happy-web, happy-server are blocked.

checks.name: systemctl stop/restart whitelist
checks.details: Lines 168-175 use check_systemctl_targets_all_dev with DEV_SYSTEMD whitelist (happy-daemon-dev only). Strips .service suffix for comparison. Production services like happy-daemon, happy-daemon-jade are blocked.

checks.name: Docker daemon protection
checks.details: Line 116 blocks 'systemctl (restart|stop|disable) docker'. Line 123 blocks modifications to /etc/docker/daemon.json.

checks.name: Sensitive file write protection
checks.details: Lines 95-106 block Bash redirects to/from files containing .env, credentials, secret, password.

issues.description: Line 287: '\b' word boundary in '/usr/bin/happy\b' incorrectly matches '/usr/bin/happy-dev'. In grep -E, \b matches between 'y' (word char) and '-' (non-word char). This means ANY command referencing /usr/bin/happy-dev (the dev binary) is incorrectly BLOCKED by this rule. The correct pattern already exists on line 316: 'happy([^-]|$)'. Verified empirically: echo 'abc-def' | grep -qE 'abc\b' returns true.
issues.fix: Replace line 287 pattern: change '/usr/bin/happy\b' to '/usr/bin/happy([^-]|$)' to match how line 316 already handles this distinction.

issues.description: Lines 161+297: 'kill -TERM PID', 'kill -15 PID', and 'kill -HUP PID' all escape the kill blocking rules. Line 161 only catches 'kill -9'. Line 297 pattern 'kill\s+[0-9]' requires a digit immediately after whitespace, but signal flags (-TERM, -15) start with a hyphen.
issues.fix: Change line 297 pattern to 'kill\s+(-[A-Za-z0-9]+\s+)*[0-9]' to match optional signal flags before the PID, or simplify to 'kill\s+' to block all kill invocations (since the comment says 'kill with PIDs is FORBIDDEN').

issues.description: Line 276: 'npm install -g' pattern has two bypass paths: (1) 'npm install <package> -g' puts the -g flag after the package name, escaping the pattern that requires -g immediately after 'install'. (2) 'npm i -g <package>' uses the 'i' shorthand instead of 'install', which the pattern does not match.
issues.fix: Add additional patterns: 'npm\s+i\s+-g', 'npm\s+i\s+--global', and also match -g/--global anywhere in the npm install command line, e.g., 'npm\s+(install|i)\s+.*(-g|--global)'.
